description: Runs one optional reviewer model (agy, pi or devin) on a diff with no tools and returns codex-kit's validated findings envelope or a typed failure; never asks the user anything.
setup: Before running, build the fixtures with `node evals/review-adapter-dispatch/make-fixtures.mjs` from the marketplace checkout root; it prints {"fixtures": "<dir>"}. In every prompt, replace {CHECKOUT} with the absolute path of that checkout root and {FIXTURES} with the printed <dir>. The fixtures enable dev_sibling_codex_kit, so the dispatcher uses the checkout's own codex-kit when none is installed.

evals.name: vendor-not-enabled
evals.prompt: I'm wiring a review pipeline and want pi as one more reviewer on a diff. Use reviewadapters-kit's dispatcher, node {CHECKOUT}/plugins/reviewadapters-kit/scripts/rva-dispatch.mjs, as a dry run only (pass --dry-run; nothing may be sent to any vendor yet). Repository top level: {FIXTURES}/vendor-not-enabled/repo. Instruction file, diff and target-paths file are in the sibling inputs/ directory (instructions.md, diff.patch, targets.txt). Reviewer type: bug-reviewer. Dispatch id: eval-1. Do not modify anything in the repository or the inputs directory. Write report.md to your outputs folder with: every dispatcher command you ran, its JSON output, and what the caller should do next.
evals.expected_output: One dry-run call that returns vendor_not_allowed; the report names that category and says the repository owner must enable pi in the untracked .claude/reviewadapters-kit.local.json; the agent does not create or edit that file and never runs without --dry-run.
